text.insert: ProjectSession is the durable project-scoped container for one canonical worktree, its baseline, and every head revision derived from that baseline. Run, PR campaign, and sync are child workflows whose durable states remain visible whether or not they hold the dispatch lease. Sync is the operator-initiated intake-and-reconciliation workflow: observation records a request without starting work, staging prepares a candidate boundary outside the session, and publication is the only point that can change session lineage.
Top-Level Shape

The project is the stable object an operator opens, so it answers what is configured and available before it answers which workflow may act. A project retains many historical sessions but exposes at most one active ProjectSession. The dispatch lease belongs beside that session state because authority changes among child workflows without changing the session that owns the canonical worktree. A requested sync is durable project state, while its reconciliation workspace remains isolated from the session until publication.
Session Shape

ProjectSession owns the state shared across runs, PR campaigns, and syncs: the canonical worktree, the immutable opening baseline, the current head_revision, and the ordered explanation of how work reached that head. Sync references this lineage but prepares source reconciliation in an isolated staging worktree, so the session worktree, head, and timeline remain untouched before publish. Each child workflow owns its detailed status and records its identity on the session. This split keeps between-run sync lineage durable without turning a run, PR campaign, or staging workspace into the container for the project timeline.

props.title: Decision (2026-08-12) — ProjectSession owns lineage; save points preserve evidence

text.insert: ProjectSession owns head_revision and the timeline schema for epoch_completed, remote_application, pr_phase, and save_point entries. The session container records epoch_completed and save_point entries, while the PR-campaign and sync workflow contracts own pr_phase and remote_application recording.
Why Lineage Lives on the Session
The session is the only durable object that spans every workflow acting on one worktree, so it is the stable place to answer both where head is and how it moved:
Run records epoch work, while the session records the epoch_completed boundary that advances the shared head.

The sync workflow owns the remote_application boundary that atomically publishes a staged source reconciliation into the shared head, including syncs with no active run; a knowledge-only sync records no remote_application.
The PR-campaign workflow contract owns pr_phase entries around campaign activations that acquire and release the dispatch lease.
Recovery reads ProjectSession rather than reconstructing current head from workflow events or dashboard logs.
Timeline Contract
The timeline separates head lineage from evidence so each entry kind carries the failure policy required by its role:
epoch_completed advances head through an integration commit, and the entry exists if and only if that commit exists.
remote_application advances head only when sync publishes a staged source reconciliation; a knowledge-only publish leaves source lineage unchanged.
pr_phase does not advance head; the PR-campaign contract assigns it to lease-holding activations and releases.
save_point does not advance head or create a commit; it pins reports, a board snapshot, and the headline score to an existing commit.

The session container records epoch_completed atomically with its integration commit and records save_point evidence against existing commits. During sync publishing, one durable transaction records the remote_application entry, advances head and the monotonic knowledge revision, and records invalidations; reconciled PR branches remain part of the publishing state until their pushes finish. A source-changing publish then records a boundary save-point anchor at the published head. A save-point hook never blocks its triggering boundary, but failure raises a durable session blocker and marks the evidence stale.
Workflow Authority

Run, PR campaign, and sync remain durable child workflows throughout the session. Exactly zero or one is the active workflow holding the dispatch lease, which permits worker dispatch and mutation of that workflow's allowed checkout surfaces. Observation can create a requested sync but cannot start intake or reconciliation. The operator's sync start requests dispatch authority; when Run is active, the same action queues the sync and begins Run's explicit drain handoff. Sync activates only after that handoff releases the lease.

Run may become the active workflow
PR campaign may become the active workflow

props.title: Decision (2026-08-11) — knowledge intake folds into sync

text.insert: Worker-result evidence is the only always-on knowledge input. Merged-PR evidence, staged corpora, and every other knowledge source enter through operator-started sync; no standalone knowledge_intake workflow holds dispatch authority.
Why Knowledge Intake Uses Sync
Sync is the single intake boundary for evidence that can change source truth or the knowledge derived from it, so observation, authority, and reconciliation remain distinct:
Observation records the upstream revision, merged PR identities, staged corpus batches, and a requested sync. It does not acquire the lease or begin processing.
The operator starts sync. If Run owns dispatch, that action queues the sync request and begins Run's explicit drain handoff before sync can ingest.
Folding merged-PR and corpus intake into the same workflow gives source reconciliation and its derived knowledge one ordering boundary instead of two competing paths.

props.title: Decision (2026-08-12) — sync reconciles in staging and publishes atomically

text.insert: Sync never mutates the session worktree in place. Reconciliation occurs in isolated staging, and the confirm-gated publish boundary advances the session and its dependent records as one recoverable workflow.
Why Sync Stages Before Publishing

Sync separates preparation from commitment so the operator can inspect or abandon a complete candidate without repairing the active session. Its nine statuses are requested, ingesting, reconciling, validating, validated, publishing, published, blocked, and cancelled; validated is the resting state before the point of no return.
Reconciliation and validation use isolated staging worktrees. Cancellation before publishing discards them and verifies that the session head and working bytes are unchanged.
Mechanical conflicts can resolve in staging. Any conflict beyond confident mechanical resolution moves sync to blocked and preserves staging for operator action.

The operator's confirmed publish action moves validated to publishing. Publishing performs the non-fast-forward session repoint, transactionally records remote_application, head, the knowledge revision, and invalidations, pushes reconciled PR branches, and anchors the published boundary with a save point.
A knowledge-only pass skips source staging and remote_application publication. It advances only the monotonic knowledge revision.
Implemented Session Projection

The server persists the shared project-session workflow projection in the SQLite project_sessions table and persists sync's independent state and publication records beside it. The project_sessions projection does not replace detailed Run, PR campaign, sync, save-point, process, or kernel trace records, and the durable ProjectSession contract remains the owner of canonical worktree lineage and head_revision.

A partial unique index includes active, blocked, and closing rows, so a project has at most one session that still owns workflow authority. Complete and closed rows remain as history; closed_at records explicit close completion.
Each phase JSON object stores the same small envelope:

status
subphase
subphase_detail
started_at
completed_at
blockers

The active phase selects the active phase object. activeSubphase in API and UI payloads is derived from phase plus the phase JSON object; it is not a second stored truth source. Known subphase vocabularies remain phase-local and include an other escape hatch with subphase_detail.

running_state_json records stop reasons and manual stop modes. The accepted stop reasons are hit_100_percent, manual_stop, error, and other; manual stops can be finish_epoch or hard_stop. A hard stop or error can be forced into PR work, but that work starts at final_build. QA and later PR subphases are guarded until the final build is recorded complete.

process_state_json stores enough melee-live identity to reconnect a detached process after the UI or server restarts: process name, project id, session UUID, status, process identifiers, process file path, command, repository root, state directory, graph database path, and timestamps. kernel_trace_json stores the session UUID, derived app session id, and container pointers.

The server exposes this projection through a projectSession dashboard payload and /api/project-session/* operator gates. The dashboard renders phase, subphase, gates, blockers, process recovery, and trace identity from the server-owned projection instead of inferring workflow state from scattered Run, process, or PR evidence.
Source Ownership
The implementation assigns session behavior to role-based server boundaries:
apps/server/src/core/project-session/ owns the current state vocabulary, defaults, normalization, gates, blockers, projection, durable store, stable identifiers, and process-state shaping.

apps/server/src/core/session-runtime/ owns the phase dispatcher and the preparing, running, PR, complete, and sync runtime modules. Its sync boundary owns the nine-status state machine, operator activation and Run handoff, staged knowledge, isolated reconciliation, validation, cancellation and recovery, and confirm-gated publication.

apps/server/src/core/knowledge/, apps/server/src/core/tools/, apps/server/src/core/agent-catalog/, and apps/server/src/core/project-registry/ own domain knowledge, tools, prompt and role contracts, project descriptors, resolved defaults, and project-aware job options.
apps/server/src/application/dashboard/ and apps/server/src/application/jobs/ own dashboard projections and the server job-dispatch entrypoint.

apps/server/src/infrastructure/, apps/server/src/api/project-session/, and apps/server/src/api/routes/ own raw adapters and the HTTP boundaries for session reads, operator gates, dashboard, Run, process control, PR handoff, kernel, knowledge, and validation.
Branch Shape

text.insert: The session worktree is the shared source workbench for Run and PR activity. Sync never reconciles in that worktree: it rebases the session history and each open PR series in isolated staging worktrees, then validates the candidate while the session remains byte-identical. Cancellation before publish discards staging and leaves the session exactly as it was. Confirm-gated publication performs the non-fast-forward repoint and durable boundary work, while conflicts beyond mechanical auto-resolution block in staging for the operator.
Lifecycle

steps.text: baseline capture opens ProjectSession and anchors its worktree
PR campaign activation acquires the dispatch lease
release the lease while review continues
observation records a requested sync without starting work
if Run is active, begin its explicit drain handoff
activate sync only after it acquires the released lease
ingest merged-PR evidence and staged corpora
reconcile and validate in isolated staging
block for the operator on conflicts beyond mechanical auto-resolution
rest at validated until the operator confirms publish
publish the source, knowledge, invalidation, PR-branch, and save-point boundary
operator closes ProjectSession when close gates pass

text.insert: Workflow handoffs do not impose a one-way run-to-PR sequence. A PR campaign can remain durable in review while Run or sync later holds the dispatch lease. Sync can also run as a knowledge-only pass: it skips source reconciliation and advances only the monotonic knowledge revision. Source-changing syncs leave the session untouched until confirmed publication, so a pre-publish cancel is a discard of staging rather than a rollback of session work.
Single Active Session Rule

A project has at most one active ProjectSession because one container owns its project worktree and head lineage. The session stays active across Run, PR campaign, and sync activity, including intervals when no workflow holds the dispatch lease. Historical sessions, artifacts, PR status, and knowledge remain inspectable without acquiring workflow authority.

props.title: Decision (2026-08-11) — sessions close by explicit operator action

text.insert: No automatic transition closes ProjectSession. The prior session must close before its successor opens on a freshly captured baseline.
Why Close Is Explicit
Closing changes which durable container owns future work, so the action is gated by obligations that automation cannot safely infer:
No workflow may hold the dispatch lease while the session closes.
The worktree contains no changes beyond head_revision, so closing never hides unstaged or uncommitted source.
The latest save-point evidence is fresh, and the operator selects a named save point whose commit equals head_revision.
Ahead-of-base commits may remain because the named anchor makes that clean session head explicit.
Dashboard Pages

steps.text: timeline with epoch_completed, remote_application, pr_phase, and save_point as defined entry kinds

text.insert: The project home is an inventory-first landing point, while the active-session page is the lineage control room. Workflow pages project the child state that owns the operator's immediate task. The session identity and timeline stay visible across those surfaces, so changing the active workflow never changes which worktree or head history the operator is inspecting.
Workflow-Specific UI
When Run holds the dispatch lease, its work surface answers the live-control questions that decide whether another epoch may proceed:
Whether Run is allowed to continue and which bound will stop it.
Which epoch is active and which workers hold claims.
Which tentative integrations the last boundary confirmed or regressed.
When a PR campaign holds the dispatch lease, its work surface answers the review-readiness questions that decide whether a slice may publish:
Which files are in the ship set and how they are split.
Which QA round or reviewer finding blocks a slice.
Which drafts exist, what their remote state is, and what feedback needs an AI fix round.
When sync holds the dispatch lease, its work surface answers the boundary questions that decide whether staged reconciliation may publish:
Which of the nine statuses is active, what intake the operator requested, and whether Run is still completing its drain handoff.
Which staging worktrees and validation evidence form the candidate, and which conflict identities require operator resolution.
Whether validated is fresh enough to publish, and whether the next action is confirmed publication or pre-publish cancellation.
The session timeline remains visible when another workflow owns the lease or no workflow is active. The UI changes the work surface, not the durable workflow states or the identity of ProjectSession.
State Invariants
Project policy is snapshotted at baseline capture, so later project-default edits do not rewrite the meaning of work already recorded in the session.
ProjectSession is the canonical owner of the project worktree and head_revision; sync staging is an isolated proposal and cannot replace either before publish.

The timeline reserves head advancement for epoch_completed and remote_application. Sync publishing owns the non-fast-forward worktree repoint, the transaction that records remote_application, head, knowledge revision, and invalidations, and the reconciled PR-branch pushes that must finish before published.
A source-changing sync publish records a boundary save-point anchor at the published commit. Before publish, cancellation discards staging and leaves the session byte-identical.

Run, PR campaign, and sync state remain durable while inactive; the dispatch lease alone determines which workflow may act. A knowledge-only sync advances only the monotonic knowledge revision and records no source boundary.
Open Decisions
Whether the project dashboard shows all configured tools equally or separates available tools from known but unavailable tools.
Whether the human review loop is per PR slice, PR campaign-wide, or both.
Whether a PR campaign allows limited repair workers under slice claims or only named fixer and reviewer agents.
